MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 27, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 6:02 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8
  -

  1. Property:  6100 Via Escondido Drive, Malibu, CA
  APN 4460-003-015
  APN 4460-014-006

  Agency Negotiator: Interim City Attorney Rusin
  Negotiating Parties: Via Escondido Holdings LLC
  Under Negotiation: Price and terms of payment

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 6:41 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tern Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo,
  Acting Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability
  Director; Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Susan Dueflas, Public Safety Manager; Rob
  DuBoux, Public Works Director; Matt Myerhoff, Media Information Officer; Alicia Tang,
  Graphic Artist; Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant; Caryn De La Cruz,
  Environmental Sustainability Analyst; Mark Johnson, Environmental Programs
  Coordinator; Rebecca Nelson-Brown, Senior Administrative Assistant; Tracey Rossine,
  Environmental Programs Manager; and Isabel Scheibeihut, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Stewart led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 6:02 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8, with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council discussed the items on
  the Closed Session agenda with no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on March
  17, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on March 24, 2023.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda, hearing Item No. 6.A. before Item No. l.A. and adjourn the
  meeting in memory of Reverend Paul Robert Elder.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Pro Tern Uhring moved to also adjourn the meeting in memory of John Wall.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and seconder of the motion.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Riggins moved to also adjourn the meeting in memory of the six
  victims of the March 27, 2023 Nashville Covenant School shooting.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker of the motion.

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.
   Malibu City Council

RECESS  At 6:44 p.m., Mayor Silverstein recessed the meeting for a welcome reception in
  the multi-purpose room. The meeting resumed at 7:15 p.m. with all
  Councilmembers present.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Malibu Bluffs Park Snack Shack
  Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback regarding the options for
  replacement of the snack shack at Malibu Bluffs Park.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo and Planning Director Mollica
  presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Ted Vaill, Dane Skophammer, Jo Drummond, Howard Rudzki, Gracelyn
  Lugo, Immy Lugo, Alicia Peak, Jake Lingo, and Marissa Coughlan

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item.

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Mayor Silverstein seconded a motion to: 1)
  authorize the City Manager to act as fast as possible to purchase a food service
  trailer at a cost not to exceed $100,000; 2) direct staff to initiate the demolition of
  the current snack shack and site cleanup/preparation at a cost not to exceed $10,000;
  and 3) direct staff to bring back a resolution to initiate a local coastal program
  amendment and Zone Text Amendment to authorize a permanent snack shack.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Grisanti moved to direct staff to return with a proposed plan for
  the operation of the food service trailer and construction and operation of a
  permanent snack shack.

  The Council discussed the motion and directed questions to staff and Mr. Rudzki.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and the seconder.

FRIENDLY AMENDEMENT
  Mayor Silverstein moved to direct staff to bring back an item for discussion of a
  policy or interpretation of the allowed uses of Bluffs Park related to the snack shack
  within the next month.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 27, 2023
  Page 4 of 9

  The amendment was accepted by the maker of the motion.

  The Council discussed the amended motion and directed questions to staff.

 FRIENDLY AMENDEMENT
  Councilmember Riggins moved to have the increase not exceed for demolition of
  the current snack shack and site cleanup/preparation to $25,000.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and the seconder of the motion.

  The Council discussed the amended motion and directed questions to staff.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Riggins moved to direct staff to consult with the Parks and
  Recreation Commission regarding the design of the permanent snack shack.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and the seconder of the motion.

  The Council discussed the amended motion and directed questions to staff and Mr.
  Rudzki.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Silverstein moved to have the food service trailer delivered by May 15,
  2023.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker of the motion.

  The Council discussed the amended motion.

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation on 2022 Environmental Programs Accomplishments (ENERGY)

  Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy and Environmental Sustainability
  Analyst De La Cruz provided a presentation on the City’s energy programs, a
  comparison with other cities’ programs, work plan assignments, Clean Power
  Alliance, and Dark Sky Ordinance compliance and enforcement.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Jefferson Wagner asked the Council to adjourn in memory of Rick Hodgson. He
  requested that the Council approve the General Fund Grant Application submitted
  by the Adamson House Foundation for water and soil testing.

  Norm Haynie thanked the Council for implementing hybrid meetings and thanked
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 27, 2023
  Page 5 of 9

  the Councilmembers for their service.

  Doug Burdge commented on the March 13, 2023 City Council hearing of the appeal
  of the Planning Commission decision and discussed how primary view
  determinations could have the unintended consequences. He recommended the
  City set a time limit for property owners to apply for a primary view determination
  after receiving notice of a development application.

  Howard Rudzki thanked the Council for its action on Item No. 6.A. He discussed
  the importance of solving problems for the community. He commended the Council
  and City staff and the community for their talent and drive.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION I COMMITTEE I CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Jo Drummond, Public Works Commission, discussed the increasing fire insurance
  rates. She recommended the City work with a fire insurance provider to help
  residents secure reasonable rates. She discussed City assessment districts and
  recommended research on whether assessment districts were appropriate. She
  requested that the Council expand the role of the Public Safety Commission work
  assignment beyond review of maintenance and monitoring of assessment districts
  to include evaluation of assessment district efficacy and consideration and
  recommendation of alternate approaches that were more efficient, effective, and
  cost-effective.

  City Manager McClary wished a happy birthday to the City of Malibu which was
  officially incorporated on March 28, 1991. He announced the annual Chumash
  Days intertribal gathering would be held on Saturday, April 1 and Sunday, April 2,
  2023, at Bluffs Park from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. He announced the Santa Monica
  College Malibu Campus ribbon cutting ceremony and community open house was
  scheduled for Saturday, April 22, 2023 at 10:00 a.m. He announced the State of the
  City event, which would be held on May 3, 2023 at 10:00 a.m. at the new Santa
  Monica College Malibu Campus. He discussed the recent storm events and
  infrastructure impacts which included flooding and traffic interruption as roads
  were cleared of debris. He stated that multiple areas identified as vulnerable to
  rockslides were being monitored by the City as another storm approached. He stated
  he and Mayor Silverstein met with Los Angeles County Supervisor Lindsey
  Horvath and Malibu issues and concerns were discussed. He stated that an
  agreement with Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District for a day use
  impound lot at Malibu High School from Memorial Day through Labor Day was
  being finalized. He reported that the recruitment was closed for the Community
  Services Director and Deputy City Manager positions. He stated that items for the
  upcoming April 10, 2023 City Council meeting agenda included a fractional
  ownership discussion item, an item for the Council’s consideration of support for
  Assembly Bill 1500, which would allow for a three-year extension of the Woolsey
  Fire property tax exemption, and a homelessness task force charter review.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, stated he was
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 27, 2023
  Page 6 of 9

  the new Malibu liaison and discussed his history with the Lost Hills Sheriff station.
  He stated the Sheriffs Department was committed to public safety, particularly at
  schools where they assigned a full-time sergeant and three deputies. He stated that
  they performed assessments of safety protocols at all school campuses and
  redesigned the school response safety program. He stated that the Sheriffs
  Department was working with clergy of all denominations on safety related to
  worship gatherings and properties.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS I COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he attended the photography art exhibit opening on
  March 26, 2023 at City Hall and thanked City staff and the Malibu Arts
  Commission for their contributions. He stated that he attended a variety of meetings
  with members of the League of California Cities and that he had another meeting
  scheduled for the upcoming weekend where Sheriff Robert Luna would be a
  participant. He stated that he had a meeting scheduled with the new Executive Chair
  of the California Coastal Commission as part of another organization he was
  involved in.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she attended the Road Race Ad Hoc Committee
  meeting, and that she and Mayor Grisanti attended the School District Separation
  Ad Hoc Committee meeting. She stated she met with Assemblymember Jacqui
  Irwin and introduced her to the Malibu area. She stated that she introduced the
  speaker at the Library Speaker Series Event and thanked staff for their collaboration
  with the County. She welcomed Sergeant Soderlund. She thanked State Parks
  personnel for their assistance with parking enforcement near the Point Dume
  Headlands.

  Councilmember Stewart welcomed Sergeant Soderlund and thanked him for his
  service to the community. He stated that he attended the March 21, 2023 Las
  Virgenes-Malibu Council of Governments meeting as an alternate. He stated that
  his two key takeaway points were that the County would increase their fees for
  services by 7.63 percent across the board and the cooperative liability insurance
  fund was expected to lose their coverage for claims above ten million dollars. He
  stated that he met with Assemblymember Irwin on March 25, 2023 and that
  Councilmembers Grisanti and Riggens were in attendance and he wanted the City
  Attorney to be made aware that they remained Brown Act compliant. He stated that
  he had several meetings during the prior week with residents regarding their
  concerns about the Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority’s activities.
  He commented on the monthly investment report which indicated a change in the
  City’s cash management process and strategy that yielded a better return on the
  City’s cash reserves. In response to Mr. Burdge, he stated that he hoped that a policy
  would be implemented by the Planning Department.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring stated that he attended weekly California Strategies
  meetings and that the extension of the tax exemption for those impacted by the
  Woolsey Fire were worked on. He stated that the workplan workshop special
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 27, 2023
  Page 7 of 9

  meeting scheduled for the week prior would be rescheduled. He stated that he had
  conversations with people regarding the Mountains Recreation and Conservation
  Authority and issues that involved Winding Way and Murphy Way. He stated a
  member of the public requested a meeting with the Council in closed session to
  discuss solutions for the City.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tern Uhring, Interim City Attorney Rusin clarified that a
  closed session could only be called for specific appropriate topics and not for a
  member of the public to speak in private to the Council about general ideas.

  Mayor Pro Tern Uhring stated that he would speak to the person in question and
  strategize a more appropriate approach.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tern Uhring, Mayor Silverstein stated that the resident
  who wanted to have that conversation would have to approach the Council with the
  specific topic of concern, such as potential litigation or real estate purchase.

  Mayor Silverstein thanked the public for their input, both oral and written. In
  response to Mr. Burdge, he stated that the issue of notification and waiting periods
  for primary view deterrninations was something that needed to be researched. He
  stated that the County Tax Assessor asked him to remind the public that there was
  a misfortune and calamity program which provided an opportunity to lower annual
  property tax bills for properties that had sustained a minimum of $10,000 in damage
  or were destroyed, until the property had been repaired and rebuilt and that relief
  was also available for storm damage. He stated that the City was working with
  California Strategies and Assemblymember Irwin on extension of the tax relief
  program beyond five years for the Woolsey Fire because of delays caused by the
  COVID- 19 pandemic and that they were optimistic that it would receive approval.
  He stated that he and City Manager McClary met with Los Angeles County
  Supervisor Horvath for the general purpose of developing a cooperative
  relationship, but they had the opportunity to speak specifically about the Campus
  Kilpatrick matter which was an evolving situation. He stated that there was a
  proposal on the table previously for a population increase of more severe juvenile
  convicts and their discussion resulted in an amendment to the proposal that
  incorporated an obligation to consider the health, welfare, and safety of the
  surrounding area.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Marissa Coughlan stated she did not intend to speak on the Consent Calendar.

  The Council directed questions to staff regarding Item No. 3.B.3.

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  2.  Approve Warrants

  68490-68588 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City

  3.  Federal Surface Transportation Program Local Funds Exchange
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute the Exchange
  Agreement and Assignment of Federal Surface Transportation Program  —

  Local Highway Infrastructure Programs Funds.
  4.  Findings to Hold Virtual City Council, Commission. Committee, Board and
  Other City Bodies, Meetings Under AB 361
  Recommended Action: Consider a motion to adopt Resolution No. 23-14,
  re-authorizing remote teleconferencing/virtual meetings pursuant to AB

  5.  Amendment to Professional Services Agreement with Michael Baker
  International, Inc.
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 3
  to Professional Services Agreement with Michael Baker International, Inc.
  to extend the term of the existing Professional Services Agreement through
  March 23, 2024 and to modify the scope of work.

ITEM 4  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None.

ITEM 5  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 7  COUNCIL ITEMS

  None.
   Malibu City Council

  Mayor Silverstein adjourned the meeting at 9:29 p.m., in memory of John Wall, Rick

  Evelyn Dieckhaus, Hallie Scruggs, William Kinney, Cynthia Peak, Katherine Koonce, and
